orbits-s2.title: A satellite in a circular orbit
orbits-s2.text: A 200 kg satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 4.0 × 10⁶ m (measured from the planet’s center) around a planet of mass 6.4 × 10²³ kg. G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg². Take UG = 0 at infinite separation. The satellite’s mass is much smaller than the planet’s.

items.q: What is the satellite’s speed at B?

mistakes.why: Value: the ratio is upside down. The satellite is slower where it is farther away: r_A v_A = r_B v_B.
Value: that scales v_A by √(r_A/r_B), the rule for circular orbits (v ∝ 1/√r). On an ellipse, use angular momentum: at A and B the velocity is perpendicular to r.

why.correct: Earth’s pull points toward its center, so it exerts no torque about it and L is constant. At the closest and farthest points the velocity is perpendicular to r, so m r_A v_A = m r_B v_B: v_B = (7.0 × 10⁶)(8.7 × 10³)/(1.4 × 10⁷) = 4.4 × 10³ m/s.

items.q: Why is the satellite’s angular momentum about Earth’s center the same at A and at B?
options: Earth’s pull on it points at Earth’s center: no torque
The satellite moves at a constant speed around it
Gravity does no work on a satellite
The satellite’s distance from Earth is constant

why.correct: The only force (Earth’s gravitational force) points along the line to Earth’s center, so its lever arm about that point is zero. With no torque, L about Earth’s center is constant, even though r and v both change.
options: Right: a force along r has zero lever arm about the center.
Its speed changes: fast at A, slow at B.
On an elliptical orbit gravity does work, changing the speed.
The distance changes from 7.0 × 10⁶ m to 1.4 × 10⁷ m.

items.q: Which quantities for the satellite-Earth system are the same at A and at B?
options: Total mechanical energy and angular momentum
Kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy
Speed and distance from Earth
Kinetic energy and angular momentum

why.correct: Gravity is the only force, and it is conservative, so E = K + U is constant. It exerts no torque about Earth’s center, so L is constant. K and U change, trading with each other.
options: Right: E and L are constant; K and U trade.
K is larger at A and U is more negative there; they trade.
Both change around an elliptical orbit.
L is constant, but K is larger at A.

items.q: Taking U = 0 at infinite separation, how does the gravitational potential energy at A compare with that at B?
options: It is twice as negative at A
It is half as negative at A
It is four times as negative at A
It is the same at A and B

why.correct: U_G = −GMm/r. At A, r is half as large, so U is twice as large in size and more negative: the satellite is deeper in Earth’s gravitational well.
options: Right: U = −GMm/r, and r_A is half of r_B.
U is more negative closer in, not less.
U goes as 1/r, not 1/r².
U depends on the distance from Earth’s center, which changes.

items.q: What is the satellite’s orbital speed?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the escape speed at this distance, √(2GM/r). A circular orbit needs √(GM/r).
Value: that is v². Take the square root.

why.correct: Gravity supplies the centripetal force: GMm/r² = mv²/r, so v = √(GM/r) = √((6.67 × 10⁻¹¹)(6.4 × 10²³)/(4.0 × 10⁶)) = 3.27 × 10³ m/s, about 3.3 × 10³ m/s.

items.q: What is the total mechanical energy of the satellite-planet system, with U = 0 at infinite separation?

mistakes.why: Value: the sign is wrong. A bound orbit has negative total energy: E = K + U with U = −2K.
Value: that is the gravitational potential energy alone. Add K = ½mv².

why.correct: K = ½mv² = ½(200 kg)(1.07 × 10⁷ m²/s²) = 1.07 × 10⁹ J. U = −GMm/r = −2.13 × 10⁹ J. E = K + U = −1.1 × 10⁹ J, which equals −K.

items.q: For this circular orbit, which relation holds?
options: E = −K and U = −2K
E = K and U = 0
E = 0, because the satellite stays in orbit
E = U, because the speed is constant

why.correct: For a circular orbit, mv² = GMm/r gives K = GMm/(2r), so U = −GMm/r = −2K and E = K + U = −K. A bound orbit has negative total energy.
options: Right: from GMm/r² = mv²/r, K = GMm/(2r) = −U/2.
U is negative with U = 0 at infinity, and E is negative for a bound orbit.
E = 0 is the boundary of escape, not a bound orbit.
Constant speed means K is constant, not zero.

items.q: What speed would the satellite need, at this distance, to escape the planet completely?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the circular orbital speed. To escape, the total energy must reach zero: ½mv² = GMm/r.
Value: that doubles the orbital speed. Escape speed is √2 times it.

why.correct: Escape when E = 0: ½mv² − GMm/r = 0, so v = √(2GM/r) = √2 × 3.27 × 10³ = 4.6 × 10³ m/s.

items.q: With U_G = 0 at infinite separation, a satellite in a bound orbit has total mechanical energy that is
options: negative
positive
zero
equal to its kinetic energy

why.correct: U_G = −GMm/r is negative and larger in size than K for a bound orbit, so E = K + U < 0. To escape, E must be raised to zero or above.
options: Right: it does not have enough energy to reach infinity.
Positive total energy means the object escapes.
Zero total energy is exactly the escape condition.
U is negative and adds to K.

items.q: A satellite moves from a circular orbit of radius r to one of radius 2r around the same planet. Its kinetic energy becomes
options: half as large
twice as large
one quarter as large
the same

why.correct: For a circular orbit K = ½mv² = GMm/(2r), so doubling r halves K (and v falls by √2).
options: Right: K = GMm/(2r) ∝ 1/r.
A larger orbit is slower: v = √(GM/r).
K goes as 1/r, not 1/r².
The orbital speed depends on r.

items.q: A satellite in a circular orbit fires a short rocket burst that raises it to a larger circular orbit (after a second burst). Its total mechanical energy
options: increases, toward zero
decreases, because it moves more slowly
stays the same, because gravity is conservative
becomes positive

why.correct: E = −GMm/(2r): a larger r makes E less negative, that is, larger. The rocket bursts supply that energy. The satellite ends up slower, with less K but much more U.
options: Right: E = −GMm/(2r) is less negative at larger r.
It does move more slowly, but E = −K becomes less negative.
The rocket does work on it from outside the satellite-planet system.
It is still in a bound orbit, so E is still negative.

items.q: Earth has mass 6.0 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 6.4 × 10⁶ m. Ignoring air, what is the escape speed from its surface?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the speed of a low circular orbit. Escape needs E = 0: v = √(2GM/R).
Value: that is v². Take the square root.

items.q: A comet on a long elliptical orbit moves from its farthest point toward its closest point to the Sun. Predict how each quantity for the comet-Sun system changes.

variables.name: The comet’s speed
variables.why: U becomes more negative as it falls inward, so K grows with E fixed.

variables.name: Total mechanical energy
variables.why: Only gravity acts, a conservative force inside the system.

variables.name: Angular momentum about the Sun
variables.why: The Sun’s pull points at its center and exerts no torque about it.

why.correct: E and L stay constant. Falling inward, U = −GMm/r becomes more negative, so K and the speed increase; r v sin θ stays constant.

items.q: Satellite X is in a circular orbit of radius r around a planet and moves at speed v. Satellite Y orbits the same planet in a circular orbit of radius 4r. Y’s speed is
options: 2v
v

why.correct: GMm/r² = mv²/r gives v = √(GM/r). With r four times as large, v is 1/√4 = 1/2 as large. The satellite’s own mass cancels.
options: Right: v = √(GM/r), so 4 times the radius gives 1/√4 = 1/2 the speed.
v goes as 1/√r, not 1/r.
Higher circular orbits are slower, not faster.
The orbital speed depends on the radius.

items.q: Why does a satellite in a circular orbit keep the same speed all the way around?
options: Gravity is perpendicular to its velocity
There is no force on it in space
Its angular momentum is zero
A centrifugal force balances the pull

why.correct: In a circular orbit, gravity points to the center and the velocity is tangent to the circle, at 90° to it. A perpendicular force does no work, so K and the speed stay constant; U is constant too, since r is.
options: Right: no work, no change in K.
Gravity pulls it toward the planet all the time.
It moves around the planet, so L = rmv is not zero.
There is no such extra force; gravity alone is the centripetal force.
